title: Preterite and imperfect: events and background

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the *indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 22. The preterite tells what happened (*fundaron Tenochtitlan*); the imperfect tells what was going on or what used to happen (*la ciudad crecía*, *cultivaban en chinampas*). *Mientras* often links an imperfect to a preterite, as you know from *cuando* and *mientras* in A2 Unit 13.

items.spanish: Mientras la ciudad crecía, los mexicas construyeron calzadas y canales.
items.english: While the city was growing, the Mexica built causeways and canals.

items.spanish: Cultivaban en chinampas y obtenían maíz y frijol.
items.english: They farmed in chinampas and got maize and beans.

items.spanish: En 1428 formaron una alianza con Texcoco y Tlacopan.
items.english: In 1428 they formed an alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan.

sections.content: Ask yourself: is this a single event that moves the story on (preterite), or the scene around it (imperfect)? The imperfect is also the tense for habits in the past, so *cultivaban*, *pagaban* and *tenían* describe how things normally worked.
